from.place: The proof requires surjectivity of diagonal evaluation of torsor sections.

title: Surjectivity of diagonal evaluation of torsor sections
statement:
theorem equivariantSections_diagonalEvaluation_surjective
    {V : Scheme.{u}} (ℓ : ℕ) {P : Type u} [Group P] [Finite P]
    (c : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} P) V)
    (N : Rep.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ) P) (x : c.P) :
    letI := c.etale
    Function.Surjective (fun s : c.equivariantSections ℓ N (Etale.mk c.π) ↦
      s.val ((pullback.lift (f := c.π) (g := c.π) (𝟙 c.P) (𝟙 c.P) rfl) x))

proof.text: Compose the defining torsor coproduct isomorphism with pullback symmetry. Its g component j(g) is (identity, smul(g)). Every overlap point lies in such a component. Applying the inverse isomorphism and sigmaι_eq_iff proves its component label is unique.

The fiber of the component label g is the inverse image under the inverse torsor isomorphism of the open range of the g coproduct injection. Hence the label is locally constant. Postcompose it with g ↦ rho(g.down)n to construct a section for each n.

Pullback hom_ext and mul_smul show j(g) followed by sectionAction(h) equals j(hg). The representation identity rho(hg)=rho(h) composed with rho(g) proves equivariance. The identity component equals the diagonal and rho(1)n=n, proving evaluation is surjective.
